articles.title: Go with the flow: do you need to filter US tap water?
articles.summary: Experts share best practices for considering water filters – whether you’re drinking municipally treated water or relying on a well. Americans have a lot of questions about their drinking water. How is it treated? What’s in it? Most importantly, is it safe?
body: “I’ve even been out to eat where people overhear me talking about my work and come over to ask me a question about their tap water,” said Kimberly Parker, an environmental engineer who studies chemical contaminants in drinking water at Washington University in St Louis.

Most Americans have access to municipal water, which “tends to be really well treated” and largely safe to drink, said Parker. Across the US, water is monitored for contamination via centralized infrastructure at federal and state levels.
In Parker’s experience, “many environmental engineers choose not to use filtered water” because of their informed confidence in the safety of tap water, she said.
Nevertheless, whether you’re drinking municipally treated water or relying on a well, there are water-safety challenges.

articles.title: ‘I created my mom and talk to her’: AI ghosts and deathslop are changing the way we mourn
articles.summary: The rise of AI-generated tributes and bots for ‘talking’ to the dead has experts concerned more people will grieve in isolation. Tributes rolled in after the death of Dolly Parton last month. Jack White performed Jolene at a London gig.
body: Run Jolene, at just under five minutes, is an earworm of a country song, containing all the cliches of the genre: twangy singer, banjo licks, corny lyrics. Those lyrics concern Jolene, the fictional romantic rival made infamous by Parton. “Somebody better warn Jolene / Dolly’s coming through those gates,” the voice croons. “Run Jolene / Girl you better move your feet.”

The accompanying video depicts Parton, clad in a bedazzled white jumpsuit, hunting down Jolene, a busty redhead with prom curls. Heaven is filled with deceased celebrities who watch on in horror – or amusement – as Jolene bounces from cloud to cloud, or books it up marble staircases, trying to hide from Dolly. Onlookers include the late Michael Jackson, Whitney Houston and Kenny Rogers, as well as Cher, who is still very much alive.
points: The rise of AI-generated tributes and bots for ‘talking’ to the dead has experts concerned more people will grieve in isolation.

articles.title: There are two kinds of people in this world: hosts or guests. Nobody can be both | Polly Hudson
articles.summary: My hosting persona is an edgier version of Manuel from Fawlty Towers. Invite me to yours, however, and I am a nonstop delight. My epiphany came between the starter and the main.
body: The problem now is payback. Post epiphany, I only want to be the guest star and never host again. But is it OK for all of us to stay in our lanes, play only to our strengths? Obviously, that’s the logical solution, which would be better and more enjoyable for everybody. But if one party repeatedly doles out invites while the other accepts but never returns the favour, will it lead to resentment? I suppose only the hosts among us can answer that. Which is worse? Feeling like you’re being taken advantage of? Or having to come to my house for dinner?

articles.title: Fast, furious and potentially fatal: why are supercars suddenly so popular?
articles.summary: Once the preserve of the ultra-rich, supercars are finding new drivers through rentals, finance deals, influencer culture and the manosphere. But why would anyone want a 200mph vehicle?
body: Many of the supercars apprehended by the Met in August bore Middle Eastern number plates. It has been a growing trend for car owners from the region to spend summer in London, bringing their cars with them (at a cost of £25,000 upwards). The orange Lamborghini that Tatman seized had Dubai plates. Most of the vehicle owners retrieved their cars the next day after paying fines and presenting the correct paperwork. The Lamborghini driver was subsequently seen driving respectfully and not revving his engine. Lessons were learned, although the question remains: why ship a 200mph car to London to drive in a 20mph zone?

articles.title: This Restaurant Rocks (No, Literally)
articles.summary: A version of this post originally appeared in Eater Today, which spotlights the freshest news and stories from across the food world every day. Subscribe now. “There’s a rock in the sink!” That was the takeaway last winter after the East Coast contingent of the team that writes this newsletter met…
body: How did boulders become the hot new decor trend at New York City restaurants and cafes?

That was until I met a friend for coffee at the location of Rhythm Zero in Greenpoint, Brooklyn, which looks more like a room in an art museum than a coffee shop. There, a large hunk of stone sat in front of a large mirror next to the counter. Yet another imposed itself in the bathroom, positioned between the sink and the toilet, as though natural absorption for dripping hands making the trip to the hand dryer. Two establishments with big decorative rocks: a coincidence, or an affectation?

But then, I found myself in Pizza 4P’s, an ambitiously and intricately designed pizza import from Vietnam for which six literal boulders were transported into the restaurant from a stone wholesaler in New Jersey. Now three spots? There’s something going on there.

articles.title: 10+ New York Fashion Week Outfits to Recreate Now
articles.summary: From cool everyday looks to statement ensembles, recreate the season’s top fashion week outfits, inspired by the street style scene at New York Week.
body: All products featured on Vogue are independently selected by our editors. However, we may earn affiliate revenue on this article and commission when you buy something.

For most, Labor Day weekend marks the end of summer, the return to office, and the hopeful arrival of fall’s cooler temperatures. For us fashion folk, however, it can only mean one thing: It’s New York Fashion Week!

With NYFW now in full swing, the runways aren’t the only thing setting the tone for the season ahead. The street style scene is making just as strong a case, and the fashion verdict is in: transitional outfit inspiration is taking a front-row seat.

Think a chic mix of satin slip dresses layered with roomy, menswear-inspired blazers, double-waistband trousers with heeled thong sandals, and a slew of statement accessories that take everyday ensembles to new heights. Statement skirts are also having a moment, from Chanel’s tweed takes to spotted animal prints. Elsewhere, industry insiders are juxtaposing feminine pieces with touches of sport—a styling trick carried over from spring.

articles.title: This Wedding-Planner Bride Married in Her Childhood Living Room for Her Quintessentially NYC Celebration
articles.summary: Colette Macari’s wedding to Matt Duggan featured a ceremony in the bride’s parents’ apartment in Tribeca, followed by Champagne roadies and a bagpiper-led procession to The Odeon.
body: Colette Macari and Matt Duggan first matched on Bumble in June 2021. Matt was intrigued by Colette’s response to one of the app’s prompts (“Pasta shapes taste different”) and drawn to her “always overdressed” personal style. Colette thought Matt looked cute right from the jump—and loved that he responded to her pasta hot take.
Their first date was at Cooper’s in the East Village, and three and a half years later, on May 5, 2025, Matt proposed at their apartment, just the two of them.

Eleven months later, on April 18, 2026, they married in New York City, where Colette was born and raised. The ceremony took place at Colette’s parents’ apartment in Tribeca and was followed by a reception at local institution The Odeon, a longtime favorite of the bride’s family.

“As someone who plans weddings for a living, it was kind of a unique experience,” Colette says. “I got to make a lot of decisions independently and worked with some of my favorite vendors along the way. Thankfully, my parents and Matt trusted my expertise.” She assembled the vendor team based on years of experience, while Matt weighed in on a few key decisions like choosing the band, the photographer, and the videographer.

articles.title: The 32 Best Matching Lounge Sets for Travel
articles.summary: From cashmere coords to comfortable athleisure, shop the best matching lounge sets for travel ahead of your next trip.
body: Long travel days call for patience, flexibility, and a carefully thought-out airport outfit. Sure, black leggings and a pullover will always be comfortable—but if you want the ease with a little more effort, try a loungewear set. The right matching set for travel can take you from the lounge to the cabin to fresh-off-the-plane plans—perhaps with a few swipes of a hydrating moisturizer and a quick spritz of your TSA-sized perfume for a refresh along the way.

Between cashmere coords and athletic quarter zips, there are many directions this dressing prompt can take; so we split up our favorites according to potential travel plans. Need to look put-together for your post-trip itinerary? Choose a neutral set in a simple silhouette that you can zhuzh up by swapping out your shoes when you land. If, on the other hand, your agenda involves taking a couple Advil PMs and sleeping through the flight, pajama lookalikes may be the best travel outfit for you.
